headline: Highest risk is data leakage and cascading error: Windsurf can read/write shared workspace files while LlamaFactory has no file or network surfaces, making interaction risks mostly one-way and moderate.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A direct prompt-injection bridge is weak: LlamaFactory has no filesystem, clipboard, stdin/stdout, or MCP surfaces, while Windsurf can ingest workspace files and clipboard content. The only plausible pathway is manual copy/paste or file handoff into Windsurf, so the blast radius is limited and not default.
conditions: IF content from LlamaFactory is manually pasted into Windsurf or saved into a shared file that Windsurf opens, injection becomes plausible.
IF Windsurf is configured to trust file contents as instructions, malicious text can steer tool use.
mitigations: Avoid copy-pasting untrusted model output into Windsurf.
Use a separate review step before opening generated text files in Windsurf.
Keep LlamaFactory outputs in a non-shared location.
Disable auto-execute in Windsurf.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for imported text.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Windsurf has broad network egress, workspace file access, and MCP/API surfaces, while LlamaFactory has no data-touching surfaces. If both share a workspace, Windsurf can read sensitive files and transmit them to its backend or MCP servers by default; LlamaFactory does not add a second leakage path. The interaction exists in default Windsurf setups, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF LlamaFactory outputs are stored in a workspace that Windsurf can read, Windsurf may ingest them.
IF Windsurf sends workspace context to its model proxy or MCP servers, file contents can leave the local machine.
mitigations: Store sensitive outputs outside Windsurf's workspace.
Restrict Windsurf access to only non-sensitive directories.
Turn off or limit MCP servers for sensitive sessions.
Review which files are open before invoking Windsurf.
requires-engineering: enforce per-directory access controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: LlamaFactory cannot write files, modify git, or run subprocesses, so it cannot contend with Windsurf's broad write and git capabilities. Windsurf alone can create conflicts, but the pair does not present a true overlapping-write race. Any conflict requires unusual external orchestration, so low is appropriate.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator copies LlamaFactory outputs into files that Windsurf edits concurrently, file-level conflicts can occur.
IF multiple Windsurf instances share the same local filesystem, git or workspace races can appear.
mitigations: Avoid concurrent edits to the same files.
Use one Windsurf instance per workspace.
Commit or stash changes before handing files to Windsurf.
Keep LlamaFactory outputs read-only.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared workspaces.

D_cascading_error.rationale: LlamaFactory can generate text that Windsurf may treat as authoritative when editing code or acting on files, and Windsurf has downstream action authority via shell, git, and filesystem writes. Because Windsurf's tool-use loop can operationalize bad outputs, a mistaken or malicious LlamaFactory response can cascade into incorrect commits or commands in default workflows.
conditions: IF Windsurf uses LlamaFactory output as a source of truth without verification, errors can propagate into code changes.
IF Windsurf auto-execute is enabled, bad instructions can become immediate actions.
mitigations: Require human review of LlamaFactory output before actioning it.
Disable auto-execute in Windsurf.
Cross-check generated facts against source files.
Use diff-based review before commits.
requires-engineering: add validation gates for model-generated claims.

E_compliance.rationale: No specific residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented in the profiles. LlamaFactory is open-source and non-runnable here, while Windsurf is a closed-source IDE with model-proxy and BYOK references, but the pairwise compliance gap is not evidenced beyond general vendor differences. Uncertainty keeps this at low rather than none.
conditions: IF sensitive data subject to residency or retention rules is opened in Windsurf, vendor-policy review becomes necessary.
IF Windsurf's model proxy or MCP servers process regulated data, compliance obligations may apply.
mitigations: Review Windsurf's data handling policy before use.
Avoid opening regulated data in Windsurf.
Use BYOK only with approved providers.
Document retention settings for the workspace.
requires-engineering: obtain a DPA or equivalent vendor agreement.
